subject.title: [Bug]: childless codex-native subagent stuck initializing can exhaust unified exec capacity

question: How should OpenClaw handle quiet childless Codex-native subagents that stay initializing before the current 30-minute lost fallback?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the right behavior trades off faster capacity recovery against false terminalization of slow native Codex subagents.

options.title: Add early warning plus state-query recovery
options.body: Surface the stuck initializing task around 5-10 minutes, query or reconcile Codex state when possible, and only terminalize when the native state is missing or terminal.

options.title: Shorten the automatic lost threshold
options.body: Reduce the childless Codex-native grace period directly, accepting the risk that long-starting native subagents may be marked lost sooner.

options.title: Keep 30 minutes but improve diagnostics
options.body: Leave the recovery policy unchanged and make audit/status output explain capacity pressure and the manual cancellation path sooner.

recommendation.title: Add early warning plus state-query recovery
recommendation.body: Surface the stuck initializing task around 5-10 minutes, query or reconcile Codex state when possible, and only terminalize when the native state is missing or terminal.

likelyOwner.reason: They coauthored the current childless-task recovery path and authored the adjacent Codex-native blocked-spawn terminalization fix, making them the best history-backed owner for the policy tradeoff.
